# October Everest Base Camp Trek: Complete Packing List

## Overview: Temperature Layering Strategy for October Conditions

October offers ideal trekking conditions with daytime temperatures around 10-15°C and nighttime lows near -10°C. Success depends on a layering system that manages moisture while providing insulation. This packing list accounts for the dramatic temperature swings between hiking hours and stationary periods at teahouses.

## Context and Assumptions

This list assumes a 10-day teahouse-based trek with porter support (duffel bag carried separately from your daypack). The temperature range -10°C to 15°C reflects typical October conditions at varying elevations. All clothing recommendations prioritize merino wool and synthetic materials over cotton, which retains moisture and causes rapid heat loss. Estimated total weight for duffel bag: 10-12 kg; daypack: 5-7 kg.

## Complete Packing Categories for October EBC Trek

CLOTHING

Base Layers (worn against skin):
- 2x long-sleeve merino wool tops (varying weights)
- 2x merino wool thermal bottoms/leggings
- 3-4x breathable underwear
- 1x moisture-wicking short-sleeve shirt (backup)

Mid Layers (insulation):
- 1x mid-weight fleece jacket or pullover
- 1x lightweight down vest or jacket

Outer Layers (protection):
- 1x waterproof/windproof shell jacket (GORE-TEX recommended)
- 1x heavy-duty down jacket rated to -20°C
- 1x waterproof trekking pants
- 1x lightweight trekking pants

Footwear:
- 1x broken-in waterproof hiking boots (mid-to-high cut, GORE-TEX)
- 1x lightweight trainers or camp shoes for evenings
- 10x hiking socks (merino wool preferred)
- 2x liner socks (optional, for extra warmth)

Head and Extremities:
- 1x wide-brimmed sun hat (UV protection at 5,000m elevation)
- 1x wool or fleece-lined beanie covering ears
- 1x buff or neck gaiter (sun protection and dust filtration)
- 1x pair thin liner gloves (moisture-wicking)
- 1x pair heavy waterproof mittens or gloves
- 1x pair sunglasses

Additional Clothing:
- 2-3x spare underwear
- 1x lightweight sweatshirt or fleece (optional)

TREKKING GEAR

Backpacks and Bags:
- 1x duffel bag or large rucksack for porter (65 liters)
- 1x daypack with rain cover (30-35 liters)
- 1x waterproof backpack cover for daypack
- Waterproof liners or dry sacks for organizing gear

Sleep System:
- 1x sleeping bag rated to -18°C/0°F minimum
- 1x sleeping bag liner (silk or fleece, adds 5°C warmth)
- 1x travel pillow or pillowcase

Hiking Equipment:
- 1x pair trekking poles (reduce knee impact by up to 25%)
- 1x headlamp with extra batteries
- 1x water bottle (minimum 1 liter) or hydration bladder
- 1x lightweight water filter or purification tablets

Optional but Recommended:
- Hand warmers (chemical heat packs)
- Gaiters (optional for October, essential Nov-Feb)
- Crampons or chained spikes (not typically needed in October)
- Sleeping bag stuff sack
- Small locks for duffel bag and daypack
- Spare bootlaces

HYGIENE AND PERSONAL CARE

Bathing and Cleaning:
- Large pack of baby wipes (primary washing method in cold)
- Travel towel (quick-drying microfiber)
- Hand sanitizer (use before meals)
- Biodegradable soap

Toiletries:
- Toothbrush and toothpaste
- Deodorant (optional)
- Sunscreen (high SPF for altitude UV exposure)
- Lip balm with SPF
- Moisturizer (dry mountain air)
- Shampoo and conditioner (small bottles or solid bars)
- Feminine hygiene products if needed

Medications and Health:
- Rehydration salts or electrolyte powder
- Altitude sickness medication (consult doctor; acetazolamide common)
- Pain reliever (ibuprofen)
- Antihistamine
- Blister treatment supplies
- Adhesive bandages and medical tape
- Antibiotic ointment
- Anti-diarrheal medication
- Cough drops (Khumbu Cough prevention)

FIRST AID

Core Medical Supplies:
- Blister prevention and treatment kit (moleskin, blister patches)
- Elastic bandages or athletic tape for joint support
- Gauze pads and adhesive bandages (various sizes)
- Medical tape
- Antibiotic ointment
- Pain reliever (ibuprofen, acetaminophen)
- Anti-inflammatory medication
- Antihistamine tablets
- Anti-diarrheal medication
- Antacid tablets
- Cough suppressant or lozenges
- Altitude sickness medication (prescription from doctor)
- Thermometer (optional)
- Tweezers (for splinters)
- Small scissors
- Cotton swabs

Additional Supplies:
- Sunscreen and lip balm with SPF
- Insect repellent (minimal concern in October, but useful lower elevations)
- Hydration salts

ELECTRONICS AND DOCUMENTS

Electronics:
- Camera with extra batteries and memory cards
- Mobile phone with charger (limited connectivity above 3,500m)
- Portable power bank
- Headlamp with spare batteries
- Watch or altimeter (optional)

Documents:
- Passport
- Trekking permit (TIMS card)
- Travel insurance documents
- Copies of important documents (stored separately)
- Cash (Nepali rupees) for tips and purchases

OPTIONAL ITEMS

- Metal SIGG bottle (fills with hot water as bedtime heat source)
- Thermos for hot beverages
- Quick-drying towel
- Sleeping bag liner
- Travel adapter (Nepal uses Type A, B, C plugs)
- Notebook and pen
- Snacks (protein and carbohydrate combinations)
- Gum or mints
- Entertainment (e-reader, book)

PACKING WEIGHT DISTRIBUTION

Duffel Bag (porter-carried):
- Sleeping bag and liner
- Extra clothing
- Toiletries
- First aid kit
- Electronics not in daily use
Target: 10-12 kg (22-26 lbs)

Daypack (you carry):
- Water and snacks
- Sunscreen and lip balm
- Camera
- Shell jacket
- Extra layer (fleece or down vest)
- Medications
- Headlamp
- Trekking poles
Target: 5-7 kg (11-15 lbs)

## Quick Actions

Before departure: Break in hiking boots with minimum one month of wear. Schedule doctor consultation for altitude sickness medication prescription. Confirm duffel bag weight limit with trek operator. Test all electronics and batteries. Verify travel insurance covers high-altitude trekking.

During trek: Monitor for Khumbu Cough symptoms and use buff/neck gaiter for dust filtration. Replace baby wipes daily. Monitor feet for blister formation. Drink rehydration solutions to maintain electrolyte balance.
